title: Microsoft Priva Privacy Risk Management: data overexposure policies for Azure SQL, Azure Data Lake Storage and Amazon S3
summary: Hold: the sources do not establish the multicloud feature's arrival default, and the auditing default omits documented exceptions. The custom-policy route also skips the Create button that opens the wizard, and the claimed permission prerequisite for detecting matches is not documented.

claims.claim: No consulted source says existing behaviour changes automatically on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: "Priva" "multicloud" "default" existing policies. Read roadmap, Priva setup, policy creation, general policies and reports; none specifies an automatic change to existing behaviour or an existing-policy migration.

claims.where: Governance controls: Both must be in place
claims.claim: Both Priva and Data Map permission models must be in place before a multicloud policy can detect anything.
claims.quote: Searched: Priva Privacy Risk Management Data Map permissions required policies detect matches role groups. Read Priva setup, policy, data-flow and Data Map role guidance; these describe user access and setup operations, not a combined permission gate on detection.
claims.fix: Remove "Both must be in place before a multicloud policy finds anything." Retain the preceding sentences describing each product's documented user permissions without claiming an additional detection prerequisite.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends testing a policy for at least five days.
claims.quote: We recommend testing your policy for at least five days to help you understand the type and volume of matches it will generate.

claims.where: Governance controls: Graph compliance and privacy APIs

claims.where: Governance controls: separate permission models; Risk assessment: Security & identity

claims.quote: To register and manage a source in Data Map, you need to be a Data Source Admin and have one of the other Data Map roles, such as Data Reader.

claims.where: Why it matters: same policies and alert queue

claims.quote: Searched: Priva multicloud Azure SQL Amazon S3 pricing meter license; "Priva" "multicloud" "price". Read the complete Priva service description: it lists eligible subscriptions and add-on requirements but no Azure- or AWS-specific licensing rule.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: Several controls the governance checklist tells readers to review have no corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: "review the IAM role", "Reports page filtered to Azure and AWS", "Track Data Map capacity ... against the scan schedule". Table: Priva role membership, policy sources, policy mode, Data Map registration and auditing only.
claims.fix: The AWS scanner IAM role, Reports location filters, Data Map capacity monitoring and scan schedule checks lack table rows. No additional row is requested; this records the checklist/table mismatch.
